entities.name: PMID:25086748
observations: A 2014 Journal of Dermatological Science study followed 721 children in subtropical Ishigaki Island from 2001–2006; 127 had atopic dermatitis and mean annual prevalence was 7.3%.
Monthly mean temperatures were 18.5–29.4°C and relative humidity was 60.8–78.7%.
Five of eight tested Japanese FLG loss-of-function mutation types were detected; aggregate carrier frequency was 7.9% in AD versus 6.1% in non-AD children, P=0.174.
The investigators concluded FLG loss-of-function mutations were not always a predisposing factor for AD prevalence in this subtropical cohort.

entities.name: PMID:17291859
observations: In 143 Japanese AD patients, FLG null variants 3321delA and S2554X occurred in 8 patients (5.6%) and were absent from 156 nonatopic, nonichthyotic controls.

entities.name: PMID:18521703
observations: In a Japanese study including 376 AD cases and 923 nonallergic controls, S2554X was associated with AD (P=0.0012), with a stronger association in AD alone (P=0.000024); 3321delA and S2554X were also associated with elevated IgE.

entities.name: FLG
observations: FLG loss-of-function variants show context-dependent association with AD: no significant association in the Ishigaki subtropical cohort, but variant-specific associations in other Japanese cohorts.

entities.name: Atopic dermatitis
observations: In the Ishigaki subtropical cohort, FLG loss-of-function carrier frequency did not differ significantly between children with and without AD (7.9% versus 6.1%, P=0.174).
Other Japanese studies support associations between specific FLG null variants and AD, indicating that climate and population context may modify observed risk.
